blocks.heading: Map of a Real
rows: A process map of a real workflow
Show the current steps and the pain point.
Mapping is core BA work.
A business requirement document or user stories
Share a redacted sample and explain your choices.
Shows written clarity.
A SQL query set answering a business question
Describe the question and the result.
Data support separates strong BAs.
A dashboard with a decision note
Say what action it would trigger.
Shows you connect data to decisions.
A user acceptance test plan
Explain how you would verify the fix.
Shows end-to-end thinking.

blocks.heading: Weak Lines in a BA Interview
rows: I am good at communication.
It is a claim anyone can make.
Give a story where your communication changed an outcome.
I want to be a bridge between business and IT.
It is the most common phrase.
Describe one gap you bridged.
I did not want to code.
It sounds like avoidance.
Say what in analysis attracts you.
I know Agile.
Too vague.
Name the ceremonies you took part in and your role.

blocks.heading: Growth and AI Behind a BA Answer
rows: Product management
Higher ceiling when you own outcomes.
Harder to enter without experience.
Data analyst
Clear skill ladder and portfolio.
Less stakeholder facing work.

blocks.heading: Practice Rounds Before the Interview
rows: Round 1: your story
Write your requirement-gathering story.
A stranger can repeat your story back accurately after one hearing. Field check: problem, question and result.
Round 2: delivery
Say it aloud within a minute.
You finish in about a minute and it sounds like you, not a script.
Round 3: the hard question
Prepare a process map walkthrough.
Your answer to the question you fear holds up without notes. Field check: clear and short.
Round 4: full mock
Mock with the five follow-ups.
You keep the same facts when a follow-up changes the angle. Field check: steady on scope change and tools.
